svg.title: Patient app AWS architecture and security architecture
svg.desc: Browser to CloudFront, which serves a private S3 bucket and forwards /api to an API Gateway HTTP API with a Cognito JWT authorizer. The API invokes a Lambda that reads SSM parameters and calls the FHIR server. Cognito provides login. A budget alerts by email, and CloudWatch alarms email through SNS. Lambda and API access logs go to CloudWatch Logs. A second diagram below shows the security architecture: trust zones from the browser through CloudFront, API Gateway and Lambda to the external FHIR server, the controls in each, supporting identity, secrets, data protection and logging controls, and the controls not yet in place.
svg.text: Patient app on AWS: everything created by infra/lib/stack.ts (one CloudFormation stack, "PatientApp")
deploy time: invalidates the CloudFront cache (/*)
Security architecture: trust zones and controls
As defined in the code in this repository; deployed resources were not inspected. A request crosses the zones from left to right.
https only to the FHIR server
no self sign-up; an admin invites users
access and ID tokens 1 h, refresh 12 h
SSM Parameter Store, set by CLI:
FHIR token and cursor key as SecureString,
base URL as String (per README steps)
no secrets in Git, template or JS bundle
no patient database in this AWS stack;
records stay on the FHIR server
S3 site bucket: SSE-S3, TLS only
user pool retained if stack is deleted
API access logs and Lambda logs,
API 5xx, sent by email through SNS
Not in place (see docs/well-architected-review.md). These gaps matter most if real patient data comes into scope.
• Any signed-in user can read and write all patients
• MFA is optional; no Cognito threat protection
• No WAF; execute-api URL bypasses CloudFront (JWT still checked)
• One throttle shared by all users
• No CloudFront or S3 access logs
• No tracing or structured application logging
• Account CloudTrail and GuardDuty: not checked
• Real data also needs an AWS BAA, a private
FHIR server, audit logging and a compliance
